sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Lele' (lel, ISO lln), sources Frajzyngier 1996, 2001.
sources.note: Lele is in WALS but has no datapoints for 13A (tone) or 14A-17A (stress features): all valueset URLs 404. No stress record.

sources.note: Bibliography only; adds Quint & Cope 2010, Weibegué & Palayer 1982, Simons 1982, Simons & Burquest 1986, Cope 1993 to the three descriptive refs.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, Lele (Chad) inventories GM 1275 (Frajzyngier 2001) and AA 761 (Hartell 1993; Chanard 2006).
sources.note: Both inventories list three level tones (high, mid, low); no stress information.
Vowel and consonant inventories only; silent on tone and stress.

sources.citation: Simons Cope, Pam. 1993. The plural in Lele. Journal of West African Languages 23(1): 73-77.
sources.note: Morphology; fn. 2 (p. 76): double vowels in the orthography indicate a tone glide; high, low marked, mid unmarked. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Simons, Pamela S. & D. A. Burquest. 1986. Some comments on nasalisation in Lele. Journal of West African Languages 16(2): 34-38.
sources.note: Phonology note on word-level nasalization; p. 34: "Tone is represented as high ['], low [`], with mid unmarked." Three tones; no mention of stress or accent (grep of scanned text: no hits for stress/accent/prominence).

sources.citation: Simons, Pamela. 1982. Nè...ba marking in Lele: a cleft construction? Studies in African Linguistics 13(3): 217-229.
sources.note: Syntax paper. Only prosodic remark, p. 218 fn. 1: "High (') and low (') tones are marked with mid tone unmarked." Nothing on stress.
